gui.reason: Surfaced on the Names, Numbers & Faces page of the PS2 NCAA 09 Studio as a table and no editor. There is no roster writer and the reason is measured, not pending: this disc's PLAY table shares 37 of its 86 field names with Madden 09's 110 and carries neither PFNA nor PLNA, so there is no name to write; its rating fields are five bits wide where Madden's are seven, and the scale those five bits are on is not established.

input_constraints: Read-only: the ISO is opened for reading and never modified; plan, build and verify refuse by contract.

Schema only: table names, record strides, row counts, capacities and each field's name, type, width and offset. A record's contents are never read, and a test asserts the point by searching the serialised catalogue for the synthetic fixture's own string values and failing if it finds one.

A database the shared reader refuses is recorded with the reader's own sentence rather than dropped: two of this disc's 582 declare a field type the reader does not name, and a catalogue that omitted them would read as if they were not there.
Bounded: at most 700 database rows are listed as targets while the document's totals stay complete.
portme: Name TDB field types 13 and 14. Eighteen fields of STRMDATA.DB and two of TEMPLATE.DAT member 3 declare them, always at a bit offset that is a multiple of 32 and always with a width larger than the record itself, which is what refuses those two databases today.
Establish the scale of PLAY's five-bit rating fields before any roster writer offers a spinner; a five-bit field holds 0..31, whatever the game shows.
Decide which of TEAM's 74 fields selects a school's colours from the 64-row PACL palette. TPID is seven bits wide and PACL has 64 rows, which fits and is not proof.
